annotations.text:
Lido, redrawn.

The big move: the four tabs on a trip (Overview / Packing / To-Do / Food) become one scrollable trip page with module cards, so you see what's outstanding without hunting. Everything else follows from that — a home screen that leads with the next trip and its readiness, a persistent composer for adding things, and group signals (who packed what, who's voted) surfaced instead of buried.

References: Luma for the event page (cover card, action row, ambient tint), ChatGPT for the composer and suggestion chips, Wabi for the floating dock and warm card ground, Family/Canopi for the trip-first home.

The kit

Sand ground instead of flat white, pool-teal as the working accent, coral for anything that needs a person to act. Instrument Serif on trip and place names, Manrope everywhere else.

Covers are drawn as flat riso poster art — no photo service was reachable from here, and the illustration style holds up better than stock at card size. Swap in Unsplash covers and the layouts still work.

Two directions I did not take, sketched so you can push back.

Option B treats the trip as an operations board — fastest to answer "what do I owe the group?", but it reads like a task app. Option C treats it as a loose board of cards you arrange — feels like the holiday, but it is hard to scan and expensive to build. The Screens page sits between them, leaning toward B's clarity with C's warmth.
